transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I keep noticing this rough, kind of sunken-looking patch on my face. In photos, or when I look in the mirror, it feels like one side of my face looks old and beat-up. People tell me they barely see anything, but I can’t really stop seeing it.
Is it just the way this patch looks that bothers you, or are you also worried about what might be causing it or how it affects your health?

It’s mostly the way it looks. I just… I can’t stop seeing that rough, kind of sunken patch, especially in photos or the mirror. It makes one side of my face look old, beat-up. Other people say they barely notice, but I do.
Is your concern about the patch on your face only about how it looks, or does it also involve feelings or sensations in that area?

It’s… mostly how it looks. I mean, I keep seeing that rough, kind of sunken spot in the mirror or pictures, and it makes that side of my face look old, like beat-up. Other people say it’s barely there, but I can’t not see it.
Does thinking about the patch on your face interfere with your daily activities or cause you significant distress?

Yeah… it does, I guess. I’ve been late getting out the door for jobs because I keep checking it. And I try to stay out of site photos now. I’ve skipped some family game nights too… just don’t want everyone looking at my face.
Is the patch on your face the only thing you're concerned about, or do you also worry about other parts of your appearance?

Mostly just that patch on my face. I mean… that’s what I keep getting stuck on. In the mirror, or in photos, it looks rough and kind of sunken, like that side of me looks old or beat-up. People say they barely see anything, but I do.
Is there anything else about your appearance that you've ever been concerned about, or is it just this patch on your face?

It’s really just that patch. I mean… I’m here because I can’t stop noticing it — in the mirror, in photos. It looks rough and kind of sunken to me, like that side of my face looks old or beat-up. Other people say they barely see it, but… I do.
Do you think that others would see the patch on your face if they looked closely enough?

Yeah… I think if they really looked, they’d see it. I mean, people say they barely notice anything, but in photos or the mirror it looks rough and kind of sunken to me. Like that side of my face looks older… beat-up.
Do you think the patch on your face looks the way you describe it to you, but not to others, because they are not seeing it correctly or because it is not as noticeable to them?
I don’t know… I guess it’s not as noticeable to them. But to me, in the mirror or pictures, it really stands out — rough, kind of sunken. Like that side of my face looks old or beat-up.
Do you think you would still be concerned about your appearance if the patch on your face were to completely disappear?

I don’t know… if it completely disappeared, maybe I wouldn’t be so stuck on it. That’s really the thing I can’t stop seeing — that rough, sunken-looking spot in the mirror or photos. It makes that side of my face look old to me.
Do you ever worry that the patch on your face might be a sign of an underlying health issue?
I mean… not really. I haven’t thought of it that way much. It’s more just how it looks that bothers me.
Are you more bothered by how the patch looks to you or by the thought that others might see it?

More how it looks to me, I think. I mean… people say they barely see anything, but when I look in the mirror or a photo, that rough, kind of sunken patch is all I notice. It makes that side of my face look old and beat-up to me.
Do you think you would feel more accepted by others if the patch on your face were not there?

Maybe… yeah, a bit. I don’t know if it’s really about being accepted exactly. It’s more that I can’t stop seeing it — that rough, sunken-looking spot — and in photos or the mirror it makes one side of my face look old and beat-up. Other people say they barely notice, but I still do.
Do you think you would be satisfied with your appearance if this patch on your face were the only thing that changed?

I think… probably, yeah. If that rough, kind of sunken patch wasn’t there, I don’t think I’d be stuck on my face so much. That’s what I keep seeing in the mirror and in photos, even if other people say they barely notice it.
Is your concern about your face something that you think about at all times of the day, or are there specific situations that make you notice it more?

It’s not every second, I guess… but mirrors and photos make it a lot worse. That’s when I really see that rough, sunken-looking patch, and then it’s hard not to focus on it. People say they don’t really notice, but I do.
Do you think that the patch on your face is actually there, even if others can't see it?
Yeah… I mean, I think it’s there. I see it in the mirror and in pictures — that rough, kind of sunken patch. Maybe other people don’t notice it much, but to me it’s pretty obvious.
Do you think the patch on your face looks the way you describe it to anyone who looks at you, or just to you?

I don’t know… I guess probably more to me. I mean, I’m here because I can’t stop seeing it in mirrors and photos — that rough, sunken-looking patch, like one side of my face looks old and beat-up. Other people keep saying they barely notice anything.
Do you think the patch on your face would still be there if you couldn't see yourself in mirrors or photos?

I don’t know… if I couldn’t see it, maybe I wouldn’t be stuck on it as much. But when I do see myself — in the mirror or photos — it’s right there to me, that rough, sunken patch. Other people say it’s barely anything, but I can’t really unsee it.
Do you think the patch on your face is something that would be noticed by a doctor or a dermatologist if they examined you?

I don’t know… maybe a dermatologist would see something if they looked close. But people keep telling me it’s barely noticeable. I just can’t stop seeing it in the mirror and in photos — that rough, sunken-looking spot, like one side of my face looks worn out.
Is there something specific about the patch on your face that you think makes it look rough and sunken?

It’s… I don’t know, it just looks uneven to me. Like the skin there is rougher, and kind of dipped in, especially in photos or when the light hits it. Makes that side of my face look older, beat-up almost. Other people say they barely see it, but I keep seeing it.
